answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: Andrew Page’s November 10, 2023 Strawman article prints the maxim under Munger’s name. It supplies no original speech or book location. The checked publisher book text discusses compounding but did not establish this exact sentence; a precise first source remains unconfirmed.

author.heading: About Charlie Munger
author.bio: Charlie Munger trained as a lawyer and became Warren Buffett’s long-term investing partner at Berkshire Hathaway. He also chaired Wesco Financial and the Daily Journal Corporation. His public talks combine business examples with psychology, mathematics and lessons about practical judgment.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: The checked investing commentary uses the maxim to explain why repeatedly trimming successful investments can limit compounding. That application is the later writer’s explanation, not evidence of a particular Munger speech. A plausible fit with his investing philosophy should not be mistaken for an authenticated quotation source. Strawman attribution ↗
